correctness.rationale: For the canonical H=sum-zero realization, the complete polar vertices are sign potentials constant on one class. Their centered squared norms equal q-S^2/(p+q) and p-S^2/(p+q). Opposite facet inequalities force any inscribed radius at any center to be at most the reciprocal maximum polar norm, attained by center 0. The max-norm sign families have zero-sum contrast spans when their lengths are even and full coordinate span when odd. This gives the four cases for all incenter dimensions. Slack on all other facet inequalities gives positive relative dimension. For balanced even sizes, the remaining scalar inequalities are strictly monotone in nonzero |S|, giving the exact segment endpoint formula. All quantifiers p,q>=2 and metric conventions explicit. A reproducible 17-pair checker verified supporting facets, full LP optimization, facet-distance spectra and tangent ranks.

originality.rationale: Compared exact mathematical implications with the complete biclique facet classification of Higashitani--Jochemko--Michalek (2018), the metric-polytope equivalences of D'Ali--Delucchi--Michalek (2019/2022), the face-subgraph generalization of Chen--Davis--Korchevskaia (2021/2022), and the publicly available exact star inradius result (2026). Previous facet formulas and the special star case are acknowledged without claiming them as new. None of the inspected works states the Euclidean inball, all-centers parity/dimension theorem, and contact count for the genuine biclique p,q>=2. An older unstated elementary Euclidean corollary or equivalent Lipschitz result is a material historical risk.
residual_risks: The result is an elementary, rather than deep, metric consequence of an existing complete-facet classification; the novelty/value claim rests on the previously unstated exact optimal-center classification.
Potential unindexed equivalent computations in finite-metric Lipschitz or Banach-space literature, or unpublished tables, have not been exhaustively ruled out.
The star boundary case is known, and no novelty is claimed there.
Independent external mathematical review and historical priority adjudication have not been performed.

value.rationale: The exact inradius and the full optimal-center family of a fundamental complete-bipartite root-polytope family are intrinsic Euclidean invariants absent from the known Ehrhart and facet tables. The change from high-dimensional p- or (p-1)-dimensional loci in unbalanced bicliques to a segment or singleton in balanced bicliques exhibits a sharp structure that cannot be read from the face count alone. Contact-facet counts and an exact finite inequality description make the classification complete and reproducible. This extends a known star-only phenomenon to genuine bicliques with cycles without merely renaming a parameter.
